body:
## Quick answer

At an Indian wedding, guests wear **festive Indian outfits** like an **Anarkali**, **kurta set**, **sharara** or **lehenga**, in bright or jewel colours. Each function has its own mood: **yellow for the haldi**, **bright and playful for the mehndi**, **dance-ready for the sangeet**, **traditional for the ceremony** and **glamorous for the reception**. Avoid **bridal red**, and avoid **all white or all black** at the main ceremony unless the family says it is fine.

This page brings together all our guides, so you can find exactly what to wear for your wedding, your community and your body type.

## What to wear to each function

| Function | What works | Colours | Full guide |
|---|---|---|---|
| Haldi | Light cotton kurta set you don't mind staining | Yellow, peach, marigold | [Haldi outfit ideas](/blog/haldi-outfit-ideas-for-guests/) |
| Mehndi | Bright kurta set, Anarkali or sharara with roll-up sleeves | Green, pink, mustard, orange | [Mehndi guide](/blog/what-to-wear-to-a-mehndi-as-a-guest/) |
| Sangeet | Twirl-ready Anarkali gown or sharara | Jewel tones, shimmer | [Sangeet guide](/blog/what-to-wear-to-a-sangeet-as-a-guest/) |
| Wedding ceremony | Georgette or silk-look Anarkali or suit with dupatta | Royal blue, emerald, wine, gold | [How to choose an Anarkali](/blog/how-to-choose-an-anarkali-for-a-wedding/) |
| Cocktail | Indo-western or glam gown | Black with gold, metallics | [Cocktail night outfits](/blog/cocktail-night-indo-western-outfits-for-indian-weddings/) |
| Reception | Embroidered suit or gown with organza dupatta | Pastels, ivory, silver | [Day vs night wedding](/blog/day-wedding-vs-night-wedding-what-to-wear/) |

Going to several functions? Read [how to plan your wardrobe for a 5-function Indian wedding](/blog/how-to-plan-your-wardrobe-for-a-5-function-indian-wedding/).

## Anarkali, lehenga, saree or kurta set?

| Outfit | Best for | Comfort | Good to know |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anarkali | Sangeet, wedding, reception | High – easy to dance and sit in | Floor-length looks dressiest |
| Kurta set | Haldi, mehndi, day functions | Very high | Add a festive dupatta to dress it up |
| Lehenga | Sangeet, reception | Medium – can be heavy | Avoid a heavy one for day events |
| Saree | Wedding ceremony, reception | Needs practice to drape | Classic and elegant |

faq.q: What should a female guest wear to an Indian wedding?
faq.a: A festive Indian outfit such as an Anarkali, kurta set with dupatta, sharara or lehenga, in bright or jewel colours. Avoid bridal red, and avoid all white or all black at the main ceremony unless the family says it is fine.

faq.q: Can a non-Indian guest wear Indian clothes to an Indian wedding?
faq.a: Yes. Families are usually delighted when guests wear Indian outfits. An Anarkali or kurta set with a dupatta is easy to wear and always appropriate.

faq.q: Can I wear white or black to an Indian wedding?
faq.a: Off-white with colourful embroidery works for day functions. Avoid all-black and all-white for the main ceremony unless the family says it is fine.

faq.q: How many outfits do I need for an Indian wedding?
faq.a: Usually one per function you attend – often 3 to 5. You can re-style one Anarkali with different jewellery and dupattas to save money.

faq.q: How early should I order for a wedding?
faq.a: Order at least 3 weeks before the event so there is time for stitching to your measurements and delivery.
